note: Every claim below has a source link and a date. 'how' says how it was read: 'page' = fetched the page; 'search excerpt' = read in a web-search excerpt of that page, open the link before relying on it. Prices are left out on purpose: check each vendor's pricing page.

facts.claim: Ranks companies by similarity to your best customers, starting from a plain-English description of your ideal customer or from your existing customers.
Lets you narrow results with phrases from company homepages (the page's example: 'rooftop unit service').
Also sells contact data with verified emails. This skill does not cover contact data.
Company Lookalike needs a seed domain up front. Industry, size, technologies and location filters are optional.
In Clay, the Ocean.io lookalike source takes up to 10 domains as seed companies. That limit is Clay's integration, not necessarily Ocean.io's own.
Apollo says you can search its contact database with 65+ filters, including firmographic and technographic filters, before spending credits.
Its company data says every company in TheirStack is discovered through job postings.
Job search filters by title, technology, salary, location and 20+ other attributes, and can be combined with company filters.
Technology usage is inferred from job postings, with confidence scoring.
Extracts names, addresses, websites, phone numbers, ratings, review counts, categories and opening hours from Google Maps.
Contact-detail scraping is a separate add-on, not part of the basic run. Check the page for how it is charged.
Google Maps shows no more than 120 places per area. A scraper listing on Apify says it gets past that limit.

The Apify Store has several community-built actors that search public LinkedIn posts by keyword. At least one listing was marked 'under maintenance'. Check who maintains the actor and when it was last updated.

LinkedIn says third-party software that scrapes or automates activity on LinkedIn, including crawlers, bots and browser extensions, violates its User Agreement (Section 8.2), and accounts using it risk being restricted or shut down.

Article 9(1) prohibits processing personal data that reveals racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs or trade union membership, and genetic, biometric, health, sex-life or sexual-orientation data, unless an Article 9(2) exception applies.

The UK ICO says information scraped from blogs, social media and forum discussions may contain personal data that individuals placed there, and scraping needs a valid lawful basis. That page is about AI training data, so read it as a signal, not as a ruling on lead lists.

The Apify Store has community-built actors that pull the commenters and reactors from a public LinkedIn post. Several say they need no login or cookies; at least one says it uses an authenticated session. One says it takes up to 1,000 posts in a run and can keep only reactors whose headline matches words like CEO or Founder. One listing was marked Deprecated.
Its LinkedIn Post Commenters Export takes post URLs and needs your LinkedIn session cookie. Its Post Likers Export says LinkedIn shows only up to 3,000 people who liked a post.
PhantomBuster's own blog lists logged-in automation as a terms-of-service risk that can end in an account restriction.

Clay support answers say its 'Find Post Audience' action takes a LinkedIn post URL and returns the people who reacted or commented, through a LinkedIn Community integration where you bring your own API access. One user reported a limit of 30 reactions per post.

Has a 'Posted on LinkedIn in the past 30 days' filter. A LinkedIn community post warns that people who post a lot are often sellers, not buyers. A third-party guide also describes a 'Posted content keywords' filter; that one was not confirmed on a LinkedIn page.

The Apify Store has many community-built X scrapers for keyword search and replies. Some say no login is needed; others need login cookies for modes such as replies or keyword search. At least one listing was marked 'under maintenance'.

X's Terms of Service say crawling or scraping the Services in any form, for any purpose, without X's prior written consent is expressly prohibited. X's developer docs list scraping and browser automation as prohibited non-API access. X API pricing was not checked.

Third-party summaries of Reddit's Data API terms say free access is for non-commercial use within rate limits, that commercial use needs a separate agreement with Reddit (no public price list), and that every new API client needs Reddit's approval since 11 November 2025.

One third-party guide says Reddit's terms do not allow automated collection outside its API and that Reddit has sued companies that scraped it. Read Reddit's own terms before using any Reddit scraper.

Reading comment threads costs 1 quota unit per call, and a project gets 10,000 units a day by default. More quota needs a compliance audit. YouTube's rules on using commenters as leads were not checked.

F5Bot emails you when a keyword is mentioned online and is listed as free. Syften is described as a keyword monitor for online communities with Reddit as its speciality. They send alerts about posts. They do not build lists of people.
Octolens describes itself as AI-filtered keyword tracking across 13+ platforms including Reddit, X, LinkedIn and YouTube.
Clay's own guide says Apollo's data accuracy varies by region and is thinner outside North America. Clay competes with Apollo, so read this as a reason to test your own region, not as a verdict.
ZoomInfo's own blog says it has 300+ search filters and offers MCP and API access for AI agents. Contact and company counts differ between vendors' pages, so none are stated here.
Cognism says it leads in European data coverage, includes all its data in every package at no extra cost, and is GDPR and CCPA compliant.

UpLead's guide says a ZoomInfo or UpLead credit covers a whole contact, while Apollo and Lusha charge emails and phone numbers separately. UpLead is a competitor, so check each vendor's current credit rules.
Company search filters by industry, headcount, funding stage, location, keywords and tech stack. Search is on all plans; combining company, people and job filters in one query is on paid plans.
Lets you add up to 25 search filters and export up to 1,000 rows at a time, 2,000 a month on Pro. G2 reviewers say its geographic coverage is limited.
Lookalikes can find similar companies or people (people lookalikes was in beta). A workflow can add newly found similar companies to a list every week.
Find similar companies: paste seed companies and Clay scores similarity across industry, size, tech stack and hiring activity.
Lookalikes starts from an uploaded best-customer list or a plain-English description, and says you can export up to 10,000 verified contacts per audience. This skill does not cover contact data.
Says you can upload a single company and get hundreds of lookalikes, and that adding a second, more typical company makes the list more accurate.
Find Company search can start from Company Lookalikes or from a plain-English Description, and filters include keywords, industry, location and size.

You give a plain-English query and a result count. Websets checks each result against criteria you set and keeps only matches. The Websets API needs a paid Websets plan, and Exa's docs say to use Exa Agent for new list-building workflows.

Parallel says its FindAll API turns a plain-English query into a structured, enriched list of companies or people. It launched in late 2025 and was in public beta when that page was written. The page is Parallel's own comparison with Exa.

Other community-built Google Maps actors exist on Apify, and one listing was marked Deprecated. Sellers' pages often compare themselves with rivals, so treat those comparisons as marketing. Check the maintainer, last update and reviews.

Sells a Google Maps scraper. Emails and contact details are charged as an add-on (a competitor's review and Outscraper's own AppSumo reply both say so), and one user said the bill came out higher than the estimate.
Google's official route for place data is the Places API (Text Search, Nearby Search, Find Place). It needs a Google Cloud account, billing and an API key. Check Google's own pricing page for costs.
Lists websites that use a given technology. Two third-party reviews say its Basic plan allows only 2 technology filters.
Entry plan (Pro) is listed with 5,000 technology lookups and 2 lead-list technologies.

Bloomberry, a vendor, says website-detection tools like Wappalyzer only see tools that leave a visible footprint on a site, and that it also detects tools that never show on a website, such as CRMs. This is a vendor's claim about its rivals.

TheirStack's comparison page says PredictLeads has a free tier of 100 requests a month and tracks signals beyond jobs, such as customer wins and product launches. It also says PredictLeads has limited job filtering. TheirStack is a competitor.
Sells a Jobs Data API with job history stored since 2020. TheirStack, a competitor, says Coresignal's job data comes mainly from LinkedIn.
